question: Should OpenClaw bundle and support this 1Password SecretRef resolver, including its service-account-token handoff to a locally installed `op` binary after the proposed path/ACL checks?
rationale: The patch is a new bundled provider capability and credential-execution boundary; source inspection can assess safeguards, but maintainers must choose the supported security and operator contract.

options.title: Approve the bundled integration
options.body: Accept the opt-in resolver trust model and obtain exact-head dependency authorization before normal merge validation.

options.title: Require an external plugin path
options.body: Keep core SecretRef seams unchanged and ask for the provider to ship outside the bundled distribution if this local CLI/token boundary is not a supported core contract.

options.title: Pause for a narrower security design
options.body: Hold the PR while maintainers define any additional executable provenance, platform support, or recovery requirements.

recommendation.title: Approve the bundled integration
recommendation.body: Accept the opt-in resolver trust model and obtain exact-head dependency authorization before normal merge validation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the closest available merged implementation history for the analogous Vault SecretRef plugin and can clarify the intended owner boundary.
